To support this mission, the Government requires a modern software solution that serves as a relational database and analysis toolset. This toolset is essential for the iSMART (interoperable Systems Management and Requirements Transformation) process and is used to populate, edit, analyze, and manage TDL message data, platform implementations, and interoperability evaluations. 2.0 SCOPE The Contractor shall provide a commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) software solution, including all necessary licenses, updates, training, and technical support. STATEMENT OF WORK C. 1. OVERVIEW/BACKGROUND. The Library of Congress (Library) requires a contractor to produce, maintain, and support the latest generation of Digital Talking Book Machine (DTBM) devices, known as the DA2 (DTBM model Digital Advanced version 2), which were originally launched June 18, 2025. The National Library Service for the Blind and Print Disabled (NLS) provides free books and magazines in audio and braille format to eligible U.S. residents and citizens living abroad. NLS’ enabling legislation was changed in 2016 (Public Law 114-219) to permit NLS to develop and distribute devices to be used for reading any format, including DAISY (Digital Accessible Information System). As part of these services and products offered, NLS loans free DTBMs for use in consuming NLS-produced audio materials. NLS-produced audio materials are distributed via NLS DTBM cartridges and data files online via Braille and Audio Reading Download (BARD) website in AMR-WB+, MPEG I/Layer 3 (MP3), RIFF WAV, and other audio formats. NLS requires additional DA2 units, consistent with the existing inventory

The Library of Congress (Library) requires a contractor to produce, maintain, and support the latest generation of Digital Talking Book Machine (DTBM) devices, known as the DA2 (DTBM model Digital Advanced version 2), which were originally launched June 18, 2025. The National Library Service for the Blind and Print Disabled (NLS) provides free books and magazines in audio and braille format to eligible U.S. residents and citizens living abroad. NLS’ enabling legislation was changed in 2016 (Public Law 114-219) to permit NLS to develop and distribute devices to be used for reading any format, including DAISY (Digital Accessible Information System). As part of these services and products offered, NLS loans free DTBMs for use in consuming NLS-produced audio materials. NLS-produced audio materials are distributed via NLS DTBM cartridges and data files online via Braille and Audio Reading Download (BARD) website in AMR-WB+, MPEG I/Layer 3 (MP3), RIFF WAV, and other audio formats. NLS requires additional DA2 units, consistent with the existing inventory of NLS DA2 devices. NLS requires quantities suffi

deliverables_scope.text: ===== FILE: files/SOW_for_F4F1AS6251AC01.pdf ===== PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT Trailer-Mounted Vacuum Excavator 1. Scope The contractor shall furnish and deliver one (1) new trailer-mounted vacuum excavator system for use by the 88th Communications Squadron cable maintenance section. 2. Purpose The equipment is required to support the safe location and excavation of delicate buried fiber optic cables and the removal of water and organic sludge from manhole systems. 3. Minimum Product/Performance Requirements The vacuum excavator system shall meet the following minimum requirements: 3.1 Configuration • Shall be trailer-mounted. • Shall be new equipment. • Shall be complete and ready for operational use upon delivery. • Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) shall not exceed 14,000 pounds. 3.2 Water System • Shall include two (2) water tanks. • Each tank shall have a minimum capacity of 150 gallons. • Total onboard water capacity shall be no less than 300 gallons. 3.3 Dimensional Requirements • Overall length shall not exceed 266 inches (676 cm). • Overall width shall not exceed 97 inches (246 cm). • Overall height shall not exceed 90 in

nd excavation of delicate buried fiber optic cables and the removal of water and organic sludge from manhole systems. 3. Minimum Product/Performance Requirements The vacuum excavator system shall meet the following minimum requirements: 3.1 Configuration • Shall be trailer-mounted. • Shall be new equipment. • Shall be complete and ready for operational use upon delivery. • Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) shall not exceed 14,000 pounds. 3.2 Water System • Shall include two (2) water tanks. • Each tank shall have a minimum capacity of 150 gallons. • Total onboard water capacity shall be no less than 300 gallons. 3.3 Dimensional Requirements • Overall length shall not exceed 266 inches (676 cm). • Overall width shall not exceed 97 inches (246 cm). • Overall height shall not exceed 90 inches (226 cm). 3.4 Functional Capability • Shall be capable of non-destructive excavation for locating and exposing delicate buried fiber optic cables. • Shall be capable of removing standing water and organic sludge from manhole systems. • Shall be suitable for field use in support of cable maintenance operations. • Shall be at least 38 horsepower engine. 3.5 Hose Support and Trailer Equipment • Shall include a hose support arm, boom, or equivalent mechanism capable of supporting and

nt • Shall include a hose support arm, boom, or equivalent mechanism capable of supporting and positioning hoses over the excavation area. • Shall include all trailer components required for safe towing, transport, and field operation. 3.6 Hoses, Tools, and Accessories • Shall include hoses, fittings, tooling, and accessories necessary for normal operation. • Shall include all pumps, controls, tanks, and associated components required for the system to perform its intended mission upon delivery. 3.7 Documentation • Shall include operator manuals, maintenance documentation, and warranty information at time of delivery. 4. Delivery Requirements The contractor shall deliver the complete system within 60 calendar days after contract award to the location specified in the award document. 5. Warranty The contractor shall provide a minimum 1 year warranty covering defects in materials and workmanship. 7.
